metadata.title: Improving accessibility in PISA: Guidelines for revising and designing PISA items

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The paper reports a small-scale observational pilot of an alternative PISA Science form (33 items) administered between April and September 2024 in seven countries, with recruitment by national centres. It does not describe the use of PISA sampling/survey weights or any replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife), and the study is framed as a user-experience and feedback exercise rather than a population-representative estimation. Because no weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) is provided and no complex survey design is discussed, analysts should treat the pilot results as non-generalizable to the full PISA target population. For future large-scale implementations, weighting would be needed to support inference about student performance distributions, but this paper’s focus is on item accessibility design and qualitative/short-survey perceptions.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes using PISA plausible values (PVs). Instead, it develops accessibility guidelines and evaluates revised item accessibility through an observational pilot using student Likert-scale perceptions, focus-group feedback, and qualitative observations about usability (e.g., clarity, navigation, readability by read-aloud). Because the dependent variables are user-experience ratings and interview feedback rather than PV-based achievement scores, PV handling is not applicable, and the paper does not specify a missing-data strategy for PV-style analyses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The pilot used an alternative PISA 2025 Science form consisting of 33 items (multiple choice and open-ended) administered for one hour with a 10-minute flexibility margin. Students were recruited by national centres and targeted three priority SEN groups: students with moderate difficulties seeing, students with specific difficulties reading, and students with difficulties focusing and controlling behaviour (plus a small number of students with needs outside these three priority groups). The paper notes that not all students completed the end-of-test student questionnaire, but it does not provide a formal missing-response exclusion rule beyond this partial completion.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report develops and operationalizes accessibility guidelines for revising and designing PISA items, drawing on Universal Design, Cognitive Load Theory, Accessibility Theory (TAMI/ARM), and WCAG principles. The guidelines were applied to 33 PISA 2025 Science items in an alternative PISA Science form that includes targeted digital accessibility tools (e.g., read-aloud, contrast and cursor/font options, zoom and spacing options) and revised item text/visual/layout features. The revised form was piloted in 2024 in seven countries (N=260) using an observational user-experience design: students completed the test and then provided 4-point Likert-scale feedback and focus-group input on clarity, navigation, and perceived accessibility. Results indicate that most students found images/graphs and texts clear (83% and 77%, respectively) and navigation easy (88%), with some remaining issues (e.g., read-aloud compatibility for visual text and lack of alternative text). The report emphasizes that this is not a causal or generalizable effectiveness evaluation and does not compare revised items to original PISA items in a controlled design.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a development-and-implementation report rather than an empirical predictive/causal study using ILSA microdata and machine learning. It does not estimate achievement models, does not report PV-based performance metrics, and does not specify a statistical sampling/weighting framework typical of large-scale assessment inference. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty, and the evidence base is based on pilot usability feedback and qualitative insights.
